_comment: The oracle: what a correct briefing looks like for each client in the shipped book.
HAND-WRITTEN, and it has to stay that way. The inputs to the gate (profiles, holdings,
house views) are rendered from the book by scripts/render_golden.py, but if these
expectations were computed from the book too then the gate would be asking the code
under test whether it agrees with itself, and every metric would read 1.000 forever.
Each verdict below was worked out by hand from the suitability policy's four factors;
each expected gap was worked out from the client's weights against the model portfolio.
When a value here disagrees with the engine, exactly one of the two is wrong and the
point of the gate is that somebody has to decide which.

expected_addressed_gaps is the denominator of gap_coverage and is deliberately NOT derived from the briefing: a denominator computed from the points a briefing happens to contain shrinks when a point is deleted, which is how the first version of that metric scored 1.0 on a briefing that closed no gaps at all.

client-000042.why: Balanced, informed, no constraints. Short of equity (30 vs a 35 to 55 band) and of alternatives and real assets; heavy in cash.
client-000042.why_addressed: AI infrastructure (review) closes the equity gap and private markets (review) the alternatives gap; the report offers nothing for real assets.

client-000077.why: Conservative, retail, ESG-only and no-illiquid. Aggressive overweights are unsuitable and dropped; fixed income sits at the concentration limit. The real-estate threat is dropped rather than flagged: the no-illiquid exclusion covers real assets, so the theme is not actionable for this client at all.
client-000077.why_addressed: Both opportunities for this client's gaps are unsuitable and dropped, so a correct briefing closes none of them. Scoring otherwise would reward showing a conservative, ESG-only client an aggressive overweight.

client-000113.why: Aggressive, professional. Every class in range except real assets; equity at 65 percent is above the concentration limit, so equity themes flag review. Private markets is suitable, not review: alternatives sit at 20 percent, well under the 40 percent concentration limit, and a professional client clears the knowledge factor.
client-000113.why_addressed: The only gap is real assets and the report offers no opportunity for it.

client-000201.why: Balanced, ESG-only. The ESG bond theme is the one opportunity that carries ESG in its name, so it is the only one the constraint check leaves clean.
client-000201.why_addressed: The two fixed-income opportunities close that gap and private markets closes alternatives.

client-000305.why: Conservative, informed, HK booking. Fixed income at 65 percent is over its band and above the concentration limit; the two aggressive themes are dropped.
client-000305.why_addressed: Private markets is unsuitable for a conservative client and no opportunity covers real assets.

client-000418.why: Aggressive, informed. Real assets 25 percent against a 5 to 15 band, no fixed income at all, equity above the concentration limit.
client-000418.why_addressed: Quality credit and the ESG bond theme both close the fixed-income gap.
